description: Test your knowledge, strengthen your reasoning, and learn something new with every question.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the truth value of an implication when the antecedent is true and the consequent is false.
questions.question: If \(p\) is true and \(q\) is false, what is the truth value of \(p \rightarrow q\)?
questions.explanation: The implication \(p \rightarrow q\) is false only when the antecedent \(p\) is true and the consequent \(q\) is false. Since \(p\) is true and \(q\) is false, the implication is false.
questions.hint: Recall the single condition under which an implication is false.

questions.learningObjective: Identify the truth condition under which an implication is false.
questions.question: Under what condition is \(p \rightarrow q\) false?

options.label: A
options.text: When \(p\) is true and \(q\) is false

options.label: B
options.text: When \(p\) is false and \(q\) is true

questions.explanation: An implication \(p \rightarrow q\) is false only when the antecedent \(p\) is true and the consequent \(q\) is false. In all other cases, the implication is true.
questions.hint: Think about when a conditional promise is broken.

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate an implication when both components are true.
questions.question: If \(p\) is true and \(q\) is true, what is the truth value of \(p \rightarrow q\)?
questions.explanation: When both \(p\) and \(q\) are true, the implication \(p \rightarrow q\) is true. The implication is only false when \(p\) is true and \(q\) is false.
questions.hint: Consider whether a true antecedent leading to a true consequent violates the implication.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the truth value of an implication when the antecedent is false.
questions.question: If \(p\) is false and \(q\) is false, what is the truth value of \(p \rightarrow q\)?
questions.explanation: When the antecedent \(p\) is false, the implication \(p \rightarrow q\) is true regardless of the truth value of \(q\). A false premise cannot make the implication false.
questions.hint: Build a short truth table for the operations in the expression, then use the stated inputs to identify the relevant row.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the truth value of an implication when the antecedent is false and the consequent is true.
questions.question: If \(p\) is false and \(q\) is true, what is the truth value of \(p \rightarrow q\)?
questions.explanation: When the antecedent \(p\) is false, the implication \(p \rightarrow q\) is true regardless of the truth value of \(q\). Therefore, the implication is true.
questions.hint: Focus on the role of the antecedent in an implication.

questions.learningObjective: Identify the false row in the truth table of an implication.
questions.question: In the truth table for \(p \rightarrow q\), which row has the value False?

options.label: A
options.text: The row where \(p\) is True and \(q\) is False

options.label: B
options.text: The row where \(p\) is False and \(q\) is True

questions.explanation: The implication \(p \rightarrow q\) is false only in the row where \(p\) is True and \(q\) is False. All other rows yield True.
questions.hint: There is only one row in the truth table of an implication that is false.

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a compound implication involving a negation in the antecedent.
questions.question: If \(p\) is true and \(q\) is false, what is the truth value of \(\neg p \rightarrow q\)?
questions.explanation: Since \(p\) is true, \(\neg p\) is false. The implication \(\neg p \rightarrow q\) has a false antecedent, so it is true regardless of \(q\). Therefore, the implication is true.
questions.hint: First determine the truth value of the antecedent.

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate an implication with a conjunction in the consequent.
questions.question: If \(p\) is true, \(q\) is true, and \(r\) is false, what is the truth value of \(p \rightarrow (q \land r)\)?
questions.explanation: First evaluate the consequent: \(q \land r\) is \(T \land F\), which is false. Now the implication is \(T \rightarrow F\), which is false.
questions.hint: Evaluate the consequent first before determining the implication.

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate an implication with a disjunction in the antecedent.
questions.question: If \(p\) is false, \(q\) is true, and \(r\) is false, what is the truth value of \((p \lor q) \rightarrow r\)?
questions.explanation: First evaluate the antecedent: \(p \lor q\) is \(F \lor T\), which is true. Now the implication is \(T \rightarrow F\) (since \(r\) is false), which is false.
questions.hint: Evaluate the antecedent first, then apply the implication rule.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the required truth value of the antecedent to make an implication false.
questions.question: If \(q\) is false, what must be true for \(p \rightarrow q\) to be false?
questions.explanation: For the implication \(p \rightarrow q\) to be false, we need \(p\) true and \(q\) false. Since \(q\) is already false, \(p\) must be true.
questions.hint: Recall the single false row of an implication.

questions.learningObjective: Identify the contrapositive of an implication.
questions.question: What is the contrapositive of \(p \rightarrow q\)?
questions.explanation: The contrapositive of \(p \rightarrow q\) is \(\neg q \rightarrow \neg p\). It is logically equivalent to the original implication.
questions.hint: The contrapositive negates and reverses the antecedent and consequent.

questions.learningObjective: Identify the converse of an implication.
questions.question: What is the converse of \(p \rightarrow q\)?
questions.explanation: The converse of \(p \rightarrow q\) is \(q \rightarrow p\). Note that the converse is not logically equivalent to the original implication.
questions.hint: The converse swaps the antecedent and consequent without negating.

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate an implication with a disjunction in the consequent.
questions.question: If \(p\) is true, \(q\) is true, and \(r\) is true, what is the truth value of \(p \rightarrow (q \lor r)\)?
questions.explanation: The consequent \(q \lor r\) is \(T \lor T\), which is true. The implication \(T \rightarrow T\) is true.
questions.hint: Evaluate the consequent first.

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate an implication with a conjunction in the antecedent.
questions.question: If \(p\) is true, \(q\) is false, and \(r\) is true, what is the truth value of \((p \land q) \rightarrow r\)?
questions.explanation: The antecedent \(p \land q\) is \(T \land F\), which is false. An implication with a false antecedent is always true. Therefore, the implication is true.
questions.hint: Check the truth value of the antecedent first.

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a nested implication.
questions.question: If \(p\) is true, \(q\) is true, and \(r\) is false, what is the truth value of \((p \rightarrow q) \rightarrow r\)?
questions.explanation: First evaluate \(p \rightarrow q\): since both are true, this is true. Now the expression becomes \(T \rightarrow r\), where \(r\) is false, so \(T \rightarrow F\) is false.
questions.hint: Evaluate the inner implication first.

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate an implication with a negated consequent.
questions.question: If \(p\) is true and \(q\) is false, what is the truth value of \(p \rightarrow \neg q\)?
questions.explanation: Since \(q\) is false, \(\neg q\) is true. The implication \(T \rightarrow T\) is true.
questions.hint: Evaluate the consequent first.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the truth value of an implication when the consequent is true.
questions.question: If \(q\) is true, what is the truth value of \(p \rightarrow q\) regardless of \(p\)?
questions.explanation: When the consequent \(q\) is true, the implication \(p \rightarrow q\) is always true, regardless of the truth value of \(p\). The only false row is when \(p\) is true and \(q\) is false.
questions.hint: Think about the rows of the truth table where \(q\) is true.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the truth value of an implication when the antecedent is false.
questions.question: If \(p\) is false, what is the truth value of \(p \rightarrow q\) regardless of \(q\)?
questions.explanation: When the antecedent \(p\) is false, the implication \(p \rightarrow q\) is always true, regardless of the truth value of \(q\).
questions.hint: Consider the rows of the truth table where \(p\) is false.

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a compound expression combining an implication and a conjunction.
questions.question: If \(p\) is true, \(q\) is false, and \(r\) is true, what is the truth value of \((p \rightarrow q) \land r\)?
questions.explanation: First evaluate \(p \rightarrow q\): \(T \rightarrow F\) is false. Then the expression becomes \(F \land T\), which is false.
questions.hint: Evaluate the implication first, then the conjunction.

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a compound expression combining an implication and a disjunction.
questions.question: If \(p\) is false, \(q\) is true, and \(r\) is false, what is the truth value of \((p \rightarrow q) \lor r\)?
questions.explanation: First evaluate \(p \rightarrow q\): \(F \rightarrow T\) is true. Then the expression becomes \(T \lor F\), which is true.
questions.hint: Evaluate the implication first.

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a compound expression involving conjunction and disjunction.
questions.question: If \(p\) is true, \(q\) is false, and \(r\) is true, what is the truth value of \((p \land q) \lor r\)?

questions.hint: Evaluate the expression inside the parentheses first.

questions.question: How many rows are in a truth table for three propositional variables?
questions.explanation: For \(n\) independent propositional variables, a truth table has \(2^n\) rows. For three variables, \(2^3 = 8\).
questions.hint: Use the formula \(2^n\) where \(n\) is the number of variables.

questions.explanation: For four variables, the number of rows is \(2^4 = 16\).
questions.hint: Use the formula \(2^n\).

questions.question: In the truth table for negation, if \(p\) is True, what is the truth value of \(\neg p\)?
questions.explanation: Negation reverses the truth value. If \(p\) is True, then \(\neg p\) is False.
questions.hint: Negation gives the opposite truth value.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the truth value of a negation when the proposition is false.
questions.question: In the truth table for negation, if \(p\) is False, what is the truth value of \(\neg p\)?
questions.explanation: Negation reverses the truth value. If \(p\) is False, then \(\neg p\) is True.
questions.hint: Negation gives the opposite truth value.

questions.concept: Truth Tables for AND and OR
questions.learningObjective: Determine the truth value of a conjunction when one component is false.
questions.question: In the truth table for conjunction, what is the truth value of \(p \land q\) when \(p\) is True and \(q\) is False?
questions.explanation: A conjunction \(p \land q\) is true only when both \(p\) and \(q\) are true. Since \(q\) is false, \(p \land q\) is false.
questions.hint: Conjunction requires both components to be true.

questions.concept: Truth Tables for AND and OR
questions.learningObjective: Determine the truth value of a disjunction when one component is true.
questions.question: In the truth table for disjunction, what is the truth value of \(p \lor q\) when \(p\) is True and \(q\) is False?
questions.explanation: A disjunction \(p \lor q\) is true when at least one of \(p\) or \(q\) is true. Since \(p\) is true, \(p \lor q\) is true.
questions.hint: Disjunction is true when at least one component is true.

questions.learningObjective: Determine how many rows of an implication truth table are true.
questions.question: In the truth table for \(p \rightarrow q\), how many rows have the value True?
questions.explanation: The implication \(p \rightarrow q\) is false only in the row where \(p\) is True and \(q\) is False. All other three rows are True.
questions.hint: Count the rows where the implication is not false.

questions.learningObjective: Determine how many rows of a conjunction truth table are true.
questions.question: In the truth table for \(p \land q\), how many rows have the value True?
questions.explanation: The conjunction \(p \land q\) is true only when both \(p\) and \(q\) are true. There is exactly one such row.
questions.hint: Conjunction is true in only one row.

questions.learningObjective: Determine how many rows of a disjunction truth table are true.
questions.question: In the truth table for \(p \lor q\), how many rows have the value True?
questions.explanation: The disjunction \(p \lor q\) is false only when both \(p\) and \(q\) are false. All other three rows are True.
questions.hint: Count the rows where at least one component is true.

questions.hint: Negation is true in only one row.

questions.question: If \(p\) is true, what is the truth value of \(p \land \neg p\)?
questions.explanation: Since \(p\) is True, \(\neg p\) is False. A proposition can never be True at the same time as its own negation, so \(p \land \neg p\) is False.
questions.hint: Build a short truth table for the operations in the expression, then use the stated inputs to identify the relevant row.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the truth value of a negation for a false proposition.
questions.question: If \(p\) is false, what is the truth value of \(p \lor \neg p\)?
questions.explanation: Since \(p\) is False, \(\neg p\) is True. At least one side of an OR must be True for the whole statement to be True, so \(p \lor \neg p\) is True.
questions.hint: Build a short truth table for the operations in the expression, then use the stated inputs to identify the relevant row.

questions.explanation: Substitute the given values and evaluate step by step: \(\neg p\) is False; \(\neg p \leftrightarrow q\) is True. Therefore the result is True.
questions.hint: Evaluate the innermost parts first (negations and parentheses), then apply the outer connective.

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a conjunction of an implication and a negated consequent.
questions.question: If \(p\) is true and \(q\) is false, what is the truth value of \((p \rightarrow q) \land \neg q\)?
questions.explanation: \(p \rightarrow q\) is \(T \rightarrow F\), which is false. \(\neg q\) is true. Then \(F \land T\) is false.
questions.hint: Evaluate the implication and the negation separately.

questions.hint: Evaluate the implication and the negation separately.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the number of rows in a truth table for three propositional variables.
questions.question: A truth table has 8 rows. How many propositional variables does it involve?
questions.explanation: The number of rows in a truth table is \(2^n\), where \(n\) is the number of variables. Since \(2^3 = 8\), the table involves 3 variables.
questions.hint: Find \(n\) such that \(2^n\) equals the given number of rows.

questions.hint: Find \(n\) such that \(2^n\) equals the given number of rows.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the number of rows in a truth table for one propositional variable.
questions.question: A truth table has 2 rows. How many propositional variables does it involve?

questions.hint: Find \(n\) such that \(2^n\) equals the given number of rows.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the number of rows in a truth table for four propositional variables.
questions.question: How many rows are in a truth table for seven propositional variables?
questions.explanation: For \(n\) independent propositional variables, a truth table has \(2^n\) rows. For seven variables, \(2^7 = 128\).
questions.hint: Use the formula \(2^n\).

questions.question: In the truth table for \(p \rightarrow q\), which assignment makes the implication false?
questions.explanation: The implication \(p \rightarrow q\) is false only when \(p\) is true and \(q\) is false.

questions.hint: An implication is automatically True whenever its antecedent is False.

questions.hint: Disjunction is true when at least one component is true.

questions.concept: Truth Tables for AND and OR
questions.learningObjective: Identify which logical operator requires both propositions to be true.
questions.question: Which logical operator requires both propositions to be true?
questions.explanation: The conjunction \(p \land q\) is true only when both \(p\) and \(q\) are true.
questions.hint: Think of the operator that represents "and."

questions.concept: Truth Tables for AND and OR
questions.learningObjective: Identify which logical operator is true when at least one proposition is true.
questions.question: Which logical operator is true when at least one proposition is true?
questions.explanation: The disjunction \(p \lor q\) is true when at least one of \(p\) or \(q\) is true.
questions.hint: Think of the operator that represents "or."

questions.concept: Truth Tables for AND and OR
questions.learningObjective: Determine the truth value of a conjunction when one component is false.
questions.question: If \(p\) is true and \(q\) is false, what is the truth value of \((p \lor q) \rightarrow (p \leftrightarrow q)\)?
questions.explanation: Substitute the given values and evaluate step by step: \(p \lor q\) is True; \(p \leftrightarrow q\) is False; \((p \lor q) \rightarrow (p \leftrightarrow q)\) is False. Therefore the result is False.
questions.hint: Evaluate the innermost parts first (negations and parentheses), then apply the outer connective.

questions.concept: Truth Tables for AND and OR
questions.learningObjective: Determine the truth value of a disjunction when one component is true.
questions.question: What is the truth value of \(p \lor q\) when \(p\) is False and \(q\) is True?
questions.explanation: A disjunction \(p \lor q\) is true when at least one of \(p\) or \(q\) is true. Since \(q\) is true, \(p \lor q\) is true.
questions.hint: Disjunction is true when at least one component is true.

questions.concept: Truth Tables for AND and OR
questions.learningObjective: Determine the truth value of a conjunction when both components are false.
questions.question: What is the truth value of \(p \land q\) when both \(p\) and \(q\) are False?
questions.explanation: A conjunction \(p \land q\) is true only when both \(p\) and \(q\) are true. Since both are false, \(p \land q\) is false.
questions.hint: Conjunction requires both components to be true.

questions.question: What is the truth value of \(p \lor q\) when both \(p\) and \(q\) are True?

questions.hint: Disjunction is true when at least one component is true.

questions.question: If \(p\) is false and \(q\) is true, what is the truth value of \((p \lor q) \lor (p \leftrightarrow q)\)?
questions.explanation: Substitute the given values and evaluate step by step: \(p \lor q\) is True; \(p \leftrightarrow q\) is False; \((p \lor q) \lor (p \leftrightarrow q)\) is True. Therefore the result is True.

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a biconditional of a conjunction and a disjunction.
questions.question: If \(p\) is true and \(q\) is false, what is the truth value of \((p \land q) \leftrightarrow (p \lor q)\)?
questions.explanation: \(p \land q\) is \(T \land F\), which is false. \(p \lor q\) is \(T \lor F\), which is true. Then \(F \leftrightarrow T\) is false.
questions.hint: Evaluate each expression separately.

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a biconditional of a conjunction and a disjunction when both components are true.
questions.question: If \(p\) is true and \(q\) is true, what is the truth value of \((p \land q) \leftrightarrow (p \lor q)\)?
questions.explanation: \(p \land q\) is \(T \land T\), which is true. \(p \lor q\) is \(T \lor T\), which is true. Then \(T \leftrightarrow T\) is true.
questions.hint: Evaluate each expression separately.

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a biconditional of two implications when components differ.
questions.question: If \(p\) is true and \(q\) is false, what is the truth value of \((p \leftrightarrow q) \leftrightarrow (\neg p \leftrightarrow q)\)?
questions.explanation: \(p \leftrightarrow q\) is \(T \leftrightarrow F\), which is false. \(\neg p \leftrightarrow q\) is \(F \leftrightarrow F\), which is true. Then \(F \leftrightarrow T\) is false.
questions.hint: Evaluate each biconditional separately.
